integrity: Complete analytic necessary-and-sufficient test reduces the affine covariance update to rank-one trace-constrained inputs and a scalar quadratic determinant inequality. The double-root construction proves the sharp noise threshold and its unique critical orientation; rational computations replay a concrete failure and the equality case. Prior literature proves generic direct-method positivity obstructions, which are expressly not claimed as new.
scientific_limitations: Exact one-step direct Crank–Nicolson theorem for two real diagonal stable modes, isotropic forcing, fixed positive input trace, and 0<ha,hb<1. Does not imply multiple-step fixed-noise positivity or extend without proof to nonnormal drift, anisotropic diffusion, or more modes. The rank-one no-noise example is not a claim about arbitrary fixed SPD inputs at infinitesimal steps.
title: Sharp isotropic-noise floor for Crank–Nicolson covariance positivity
